body:
N-39 FIX ROUND on PR #119, 20 Nov 2026 (helper-n39s). Built, not walked; fakes only, nothing run on a device, VM 108 or the network. Each fix has a test seen RED on the old code; every guard mutated in a throwaway copy.

1) THE STOP'S LATE WORD AFTER RESUME. Per task id the manager counts the attempts its own Stop cancelled (memory only; written BEFORE the cancel, taken back when the downloader answered it had no such task: DownloadTransport.cancel now returns bool, read in BDPlugin.kt; forgotten when the song is removed) and spends one on the first canceled, failed or complete that comes. Spent canceled/failed = swallowed (row and place stay, no back-off); a canceled for an id we did NOT cancel is still PR 113's outside cancel (tested). COMPLETE was measured first: the old attempt's complete after Resume freed the place while Resume's transfer ran, so the pump started a song over the limit ({t2,t3} at limit 2). My first fix (keep the place) leaked it for ever (the new transfer's own completion is ignored as a stale word for a song that has its copy). Now the redundant transfer is cancelled the same counted way before the completion hands the place on. Running transfers never exceed the limit in the three tests.
COVERED: the Stop's own canceled, failed, complete; Stop-Resume-Stop (a count); the start-of-app cancel; Remove forgetting the memory. STAYS N-45's (a task id per attempt in the row, NOT built): a word that outlives the process, an old word of an id no Stop of ours cancelled (_delete, a reset, the old build's Cancel), and telling two attempts of one id apart. ALSO read in BDPlugin.kt: work is enqueued as plain work tagged taskId=<id> and a cancel sends one canceled for EVERY unfinished work under the tag, so an id cancelled before can answer with more than one word: the extra one is absorbed by the second layer while stopped, exactness is N-45's (PB-F22 and the cancel doc say so).

2) THE REMOVE QUESTION IS TRUE WHEN ANSWERED. The dialog is a Consumer on downloadPinStateProvider(target) (the line's own source, extracted): songs that land while the sheet or the dialog is open are in the sentence; the removal takes the download as it is at the confirm. The root navigator and Stop/Resume/Retry are taken BEFORE the sheet, so the button gone no longer drops the choice (Remove returned silently, Stop threw). Settings trash and the catalogue's onRemove likewise. Limit: while a release is still being saved there is no live source.

3) A RELEASE IS STOPPED WHEN ANY PINNED SONG IS HELD. One rule, releaseIsStopped (line, button, card, keep controller: no keep/ask). Resume writes only the stopped pins (one transaction). The old keep test that held 'every' was turned round on purpose. No frame draws the mixed state: it reads Stopped + Resume.

4) REMOVE DELETES THE .new of a refresh a Stop left (only the removed songs' files, after a restart too: names worked out from the extensions a transfer can have used). A Stop still deletes nothing (mutation red).

5) LABEL: 'Stopped, 12 of 217 on this phone. Tap for options', from DownloadStopWords.stoppedButton; the test pins the exact string (the drawing has no trailing full stop).

MUTATIONS CAUGHT: late word 9 (canceled/failed not spent, flag, not-in-flight counted, plain cancel in start, unanswered cancel counted, redundant transfer kept, Remove keeps memory, spend all); Remove 4 (no .new, wrong song, no extension names, Stop deletes: the original pin-3 test now goes red too); question 5; release 4; label 1.
Five older tests set acknowledgeCancels (the first canceled after a Stop is by design the Stop's own ack): none weakened, said in the PR. PB-44 and the PR say exactly: "Interrupted before it finished." is ONLY for an outside cancel. WALK ROW extended (PB-44, PR): Stop/Resume pressed fast on a real phone, long album.
QUESTIONS: the mixed release (no frame); the label has no trailing full stop; cancel() returns a bool.
